Unavailable values are left empty, and missing days aren't filled in
field.instance: A random research instance ID created after you agree, used to link this instance's collection, capacity and participation status; it changes when you turn sharing on again and doesn't use machine fingerprints or diagnostic IDs
field.participation: Whether sharing is on, the contact status (at most once a day), version and last contact time, plus snapshot ID, field version, raw and compressed size, and preparation and delivery status. When you turn it off, the background tries once to send a minimal off status with no snapshot details. Being offline, uninstalling and failed sends don't count as turning it off, and the number of instances isn't the number of people

librarySharing.notice: Uploads collection, preference and capacity summaries with direct identifiers removed, and links participation status with a random research instance ID. When on, it makes contact at most once a day; when you turn it off, the background tries once to send a minimal off status and then stops. Days with playback activity don't cover all daily use; capacity and participation status contain no new paths, videos or account details.

field.usage: Peach version, distribution (Windows or macOS app, Docker, wheel or source), operating system type and version, CPU architecture and core count, memory tier, Python version, runtime environment and public build number; at most one activity log and one daily session summary per day. Turning it on creates a random technical instance ID, separate from the research ID, to count affected instances and upgrade paths; turning it off removes the ID from this device, and turning it on again creates a new one. Continuous running is counted per UTC day and represents running instances, not people, real sessions, or whether anyone used it that day.
field.errors: Diagnostic details: the failing step, exception chain, file names, function names and line numbers in Peach and allowlisted frameworks, structured error codes, media tool failure categories, allowlisted browser exception types and release script build mapping, client browser brand, major version and OS family, HTTP method, route template and related error ID, and how often the same failure happened with its date. Full diagnostics for the same failure in the same version are uploaded only once, at most 5 a day; all occurrences are merged into a count log every 6 hours or on exit. Environment conditions such as a drive going offline, missing or damaged media, a full disk, timeouts and a busy database only report the category, code location and count, without full diagnostics.

remoteReporting.notice: Sent to Sentry. Error text, full logs, diagnostic ZIPs, media names, paths, URLs, watch history and credentials aren't reported. The receiving service sees the connecting IP. Turning it off stops new sends; information already sent can't be withdrawn.

comment.header:
Peach settings file. Priority: environment variables > this file > built-in defaults. Restart the server after editing by hand.
This file lives in the Peach data directory, which is set by PEACH_DATA_ROOT or the peach-data directory next to the project.
Docker: this file is /data/config.toml. Keep /data on a volume and keep that volume when you recreate the container.
In Docker, /media is the media directory inside the container; Compose mounts the host directory there.
Docker deployment guide: https://github.com/peach-mitao/peach/blob/master/docs/DOCKER.md
Created by: peach init (Peach data directory: {{dataRoot}})
comment.directories:
Subdirectories of the Peach data directory, such as database and logs. Omitted keys use a directory of the same name.
Absolute paths also work. In Docker, relative directories are under /data; other directories need their own mount to keep their data.
comment.locations:
Usually you only enter the real directories under Media directories on the web page; Peach keeps this table and [media.mounts] up to date when it saves.
The notes below are for editing by hand. Existing videos are found through this table; a value that doesn't match makes them unreadable.
Keys such as local, 115 and pikpak name the storage; values are the directory prefixes of video paths in the database.
The Peach database stores Windows-style paths on every system, for example R:\media\a.mp4.
So Docker, Linux and macOS use this table too; R:\media doesn't need to exist on those systems.
Example: this table has local = 'R:\media' and [media.mounts] has local = '/media'.
Peach turns R:\media\a.mp4 from the database into /media/a.mp4 before reading the file.
This table must match the paths in the database. When you move the real directory on Docker, Linux or macOS, keep this table and change [media.mounts].
Windows example: local = ['D:\Videos', 'E:\Movies'] uses the media directories on this device directly.
comment.libraries:
Directory prefix from [media.locations] -> library name shown in the interface. Without an entry, the directory name is used.
The name and path tables mirror the identity settings for compatibility; library ownership follows library_catalog and storage_roots.
comment.libraryIcons:
Directory prefix from [media.locations] -> library icon. Values are icon names from peach.media_libraries.LIBRARY_ICONS;
unknown values are ignored: a library on one storage falls back to that storage's icon, one spanning several uses database.
comment.costs: Directory prefix from [media.locations] -> proxy traffic protection. free turns it off, metered turns it on.
comment.mounts:
Uses the same storage keys as [media.locations]; values are the directories Peach actually reads files from.
In Docker, use paths inside the container, for example local = '/media'; set the host directory in the Compose volumes.
Linux and macOS also use absolute paths on this device, for example /mnt/media or /Volumes/Media.
When a storage has several directories, write arrays in both tables with the same number and order of directories.
Docker, Linux and macOS must provide the real directory, or that storage's media files can't be read; media records are kept.
Windows reads the directories in [media.locations] directly and doesn't need this table.
comment.server:
In Docker the server always listens on 0.0.0.0:8900; Compose sets the host address and port.
host and port here apply when running peach serve directly; Docker entry arguments take priority.
mdns_name must be unique on the LAN: two machines with the same name take it from each other.
review_writer_origin is the address of the device allowed to change the database; read-only devices get items to review through it.
Leave it empty to not show the other device's items to review on this device.
comment.replication:
Database replication between two computers (ADR-0017): only one may change the database, the other is read-only.
Single-machine and standalone Docker deployments keep enabled = false.
When off, the sync watcher doesn't start, SMB isn't probed, and the desktop tray hides the database menu items.
shared_root is where the two computers exchange database copies; empty uses peach-sync next to the Peach data directory.
smb_* connects to the other computer's shared directory; leave them empty to not connect.
comment.tunnel:
Cloudflare Tunnel is off by default; set an access password before turning it on.
With binary empty, cloudflared is looked up in the bundled package, PEACH_CLOUDFLARED, then PATH.
mode = "quick" is a temporary link with a random address; "named" uses your own named tunnel, only in a source
checkout, and needs hostname (the public hostname bound in Cloudflare) and token (the tunnel token).
token is a credential: this file is the only place it's kept. Don't copy it elsewhere or commit it to Git.

why.fanbox: Public lists work without signing in. When FANBOX's verification page blocks a post, a browser session gets the text, all images, and external links.
why.gofile: Used to expand Gofile pages into their image and video lists. Gofile currently requires Premium for the contents API; without it, the page link is still kept.
why.iwara: Public videos work without signing in. Restricted videos need an account with access and valid credentials.
why.rule34xxx: The website sits behind a Cloudflare CAPTCHA. Peach doesn't bypass CAPTCHAs, so it uses the official API.
why.f95zone: Finding updates works without signing in. Only attachments and masked download links need a session.
why.simpcity: The site doesn't let guests read threads, so checking for updates needs a signed-in session. DDoS-Guard doesn't challenge a standard desktop browser identity, and Peach solves no challenges: an expired cookie is reported as is.

howto.fanbox: Sign in to FANBOX, then copy the full Cookie request header from a successful api.fanbox.cc/post.info request.
howto.gofile: Sign in to a Premium Gofile account and copy the API token from the profile page.
howto.iwara: Sign in to Iwara, then copy the value after Bearer in the Authorization header of a successful apiq.iwara.tv/video request into access_token. Copy it again when the token expires.
howto.rule34xxx: Sign in, generate an API key in account settings, and put user_id and api_key in the credentials file.
howto.f95zone: Sign in, copy the full Cookie request header from the browser, and put it in the cookie field of the credentials file.
howto.simpcity: Sign in, copy the full Cookie request header from the browser, and put it in the cookie field of the credentials file.
